answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a cedar as the anchor of the cost.
